Subject: Production spike after v2.3-q profile deploy — immediate help needed

Irene,

We rolled the model upgrade (v2.3 + new qprofile) this morning per the schedule and within ~30 minutes our p95/p99 latencies jumped dramatically and we started seeing 5xx error spikes. Throughput to our endpoints dropped to ~40% of normal as calls time out or are retried. This is customer-facing; we have escalations from two large accounts already.

Attached are a sampling of failed requests and a short trace showing the p95 spike. Can Redwood either: a) roll back the qprofile for our production model immediately, or b) provide emergency capacity/fallback to the previous model variant? We need an exec-level contact now — this is critical to our SLAs.

Thanks,
Danielle

Subject: Re: Production spike after v2.3-q profile deploy — initial triage

On Thu, Nov 19, 2026 at 08:15, Irene Choi wrote:
> Folks — looping you in. Hightower is seeing a p95/p99 latency and 5xx surge immediately after the v2.3 + qprofile rollout.

Quick summary of what I see from the telemetry we pulled (preliminary):
- There is a pronounced increase in GPU memory pressure and kernel eviction activity on the nodes serving Hightower after the qprofile switch.
- KV cache hit-rate dropped ~22% for long-prefix prompts; this increases repeated decode costs and leads to longer tail latencies.
- We are observing a small class of decode hangs that result in 5xx after the request timeout threshold (internal error path triggered by kernel reschedule).

Hypothesis: the new qprofile increases per-batch memory working set slightly; combined with Hightower's long-sequence workload this pushes the nodes into thrash under our current batch/concurrency configuration.

Immediate action I recommend (safe/fast):
1) Canary rollback to previous quant profile for the Hightower production model (v2.2-qlegacy) — targeted to their pool only.
2) Temporarily reduce max concurrency on affected nodes to lower tail variance while we validate rollback.
3) If rollback not accepted, spin up fallback dedicated capacity (hot spare) with v2.2-qlegacy in us-west-2.

Attaching trace excerpt and kvcache dump that illustrate the hit-rate drop.

Rishi
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Production spike after v2.3-q profile deploy — executive summary & next steps

Danielle / Tom — thanks for the bridge this afternoon. Summary and agreed actions for record: 

1) Root cause (prelim): regression introduced by v2.3 qprofile under long-sequence workloads -> increased working set + KV cache miss spike -> GPU thrash -> tail latency and 5xx surge.
2) Actions taken: canary rollback initiated at 09:20 PST -> promoted to 100% at 09:36 PST. Observed p95 return to baseline within ~6 minutes of full promotion. Dedicated hot-spare in us-west-2 kept warm but not promoted.
3) Commercial: Vivek approved a pro-rated credit for impacted window (pending final calculation).
4) Follow-ups:
   - Rishi to run a full postmortem and qprofile regression test for long-sequence patterns by 2026-11-24.
   - Engineering to add an automated canary rollback runbook and a hot-spare playbook for customers with high long-sequence workloads (owner: Irene).
   - Marissa to draft customer-facing post-incident note and coordinate credit details (owner: Marissa).

Attachments: grafana p95 snapshot for the day.

We've looped in product and infra for permanent mitigations. We'll share the postmortem and next steps once complete.

Irene Choi
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
